name: Teeth falling out
title: Dreaming of teeth falling out
description: What it can mean to dream your teeth are falling out, crumbling or loose: common themes, questions to reflect on, and related dreams.
intro: Teeth dreams are among the most common dreams people report. They often feel vivid and physical: a tooth wobbles, crumbles, or a mouthful of teeth spills into your hand. Most people wake up relieved, and a little unsettled.
themes: Appearance and how others see you
Teeth are part of the face we show the world. The dream may echo worry about being judged, embarrassed or caught off guard.
Losing control
Something falling apart without warning can mirror a situation that feels like it is slipping, such as work, money or a relationship.
Saying the wrong thing
Teeth and mouth are tied to speech. Some people notice these dreams after a conversation they regret, or one they are avoiding.
Change and transition
We lose teeth as children when we grow. The dream can show up during a big change, even a welcome one.
questions: Was there a moment this week where you felt exposed or judged?
Is there something you want to say but have been holding back?
Did the dream feel frightening, embarrassing, or strangely calm?

name: Being chased
title: Dreaming of being chased
description: Why you might dream about being chased or hunted, what the chaser can represent, and questions that help you make sense of it.
intro: Being chased is one of the most widely shared dream themes. The pursuer might be a stranger, an animal, a shadow, or someone you know. The feeling of running, hiding and never quite escaping often lingers after waking.
themes: Avoidance
Many people link chase dreams to something they are putting off, like a decision, a conversation or a feeling they would rather not face.
Stress and pressure
Deadlines, bills and obligations can show up as something that keeps gaining on you no matter how fast you go.
Who the chaser is
A known person can point to tension with them, or with a quality they represent. A faceless chaser often feels more like general anxiety.
Turning around
Some people find that when they face the chaser in a later dream, it shrinks or changes. That shift can mirror progress in waking life.
questions: What, if anything, have you been avoiding lately?
Did you recognise the chaser, or what it reminded you of?
Did you escape, hide, or get caught, and how did that feel?

name: Falling
title: Dreaming of falling
description: What dreams about falling can mean, why you sometimes jolt awake, and questions to reflect on after a falling dream.
intro: Falling dreams are common and often brief. You slip off a ledge, a floor gives way, or you simply drop through the air, sometimes waking with a jolt just before you land.
themes: Insecurity
Falling can reflect a sense that something you relied on is no longer solid under you.
Letting go
Not every falling dream is frightening. Some people describe a floating calm, which can mirror accepting something outside their control.
Failure or a setback
The image of falling short or falling behind can show up after a disappointment or when you fear one.
The body falling asleep
The sudden jerk many people feel, called a hypnic jerk, is a normal muscle twitch as the body relaxes. The dream may simply wrap a story around it.
questions: Did the fall feel terrifying, or strangely peaceful?
Is there an area of life where you feel unsupported right now?
Did you land, or wake before you did?

name: Flying
title: Dreaming of flying
description: What flying dreams can mean, from freedom and confidence to escape, plus how flying dreams link to lucid dreaming.
intro: Flying dreams are often some of the most joyful dreams people remember. You might soar over cities, glide just above the ground, or struggle to stay up. Many lucid dreamers say flying is the first thing they try once they realise they are dreaming.
themes: Freedom
Rising above everything can reflect a sense of release, or a wish for more of it.
Confidence and perspective
Seeing the world from above can echo a moment where things finally make sense or feel within reach.
Escape
Sometimes flying is about getting away from something below. Notice what you were leaving behind.
Struggling to stay up
Flying that keeps failing, or needs huge effort, can mirror goals that feel close but hard to sustain.
questions: Was flying easy, or did you have to work to stay in the air?
Where were you going, or what were you leaving?
Did you realise you were dreaming while it happened?

name: Snakes
title: Dreaming of snakes
description: What it can mean to dream of snakes, including snake bites, many snakes, or a calm snake, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: Snakes appear in dreams across nearly every culture and era. Depending on the person, a dream snake can feel threatening, fascinating, or oddly calm. How you felt about it matters more than the snake itself.
themes: A hidden threat
Snakes can stand for something you sense but cannot quite see, such as a worry, a person you don't fully trust, or a risk you are ignoring.
Transformation
Snakes shed their skin, and many traditions link them with renewal, healing and change.
Fear itself
If you are afraid of snakes when awake, the dream may simply be how your mind dresses up any fear.
Being bitten
A bite can feel like a wake-up call, or like being hurt by something you let get too close.
questions: Were you afraid of the snake, or curious about it?
Is there a person or situation that feels a little untrustworthy right now?
Is something in your life shedding its old skin?

name: Drowning
title: Dreaming of drowning
description: What drowning dreams can mean, from feeling overwhelmed to emotional overload, and questions to help you reflect.
intro: Drowning dreams can be among the most distressing dreams to wake from. You may be pulled under, unable to reach the surface, or watching someone else struggle in the water.
themes: Feeling overwhelmed
Many people connect drowning dreams with a sense of being in over their head, at work, at home or with money.
Strong emotions
Water often stands for feelings. Going under can mirror emotions that feel too big to hold.
Needing help
If you were reaching for someone or something, the dream may point to support you want but have not asked for.
Surviving
If you reached the surface or learned to breathe underwater, notice that. It can mirror resilience you already have.
questions: Where in life do you feel in over your head?
Was anyone there to help, and did you call for them?
How did the dream end?

name: Being naked in public
title: Dreaming of being naked in public
description: Why you might dream of being naked in public, at school or work, and what the reactions of others in the dream can mean.
intro: Suddenly realising you are naked, or half dressed, in front of other people is a classic dream. Interestingly, in many of these dreams nobody else seems to notice.
themes: Vulnerability
Being seen without the usual cover can mirror feeling exposed, perhaps in a new job, a new relationship or after sharing something personal.
Fear of being found out
Some people link these dreams with impostor feelings, the worry that others will discover you are not as prepared as you seem.
Nobody noticing
If others did not react, the dream may be hinting that the fear is bigger in your head than in reality.
Authenticity
For a few people the dream feels freeing, a sign of being comfortable just as they are.
questions: Did anyone in the dream notice, or was it only you?
Where do you feel unprepared or on show right now?
Was the feeling shame, panic, or something lighter?

name: Being late or missing a flight
title: Dreaming of being late or missing a flight
description: What dreams about running late, missing a train, bus or flight can mean, and questions to reflect on.
intro: You are rushing for a flight, a train or an important event, and every obstacle conspires to make you late. Bags won't close, roads loop back, the clock jumps forward. These dreams are frustrating and very common.
themes: Missed opportunities
The dream may echo a worry that a chance is slipping past, or that you are behind where you think you should be.
Overcommitment
When there is too much to do, the mind can turn it into a race you cannot win.
Transitions
Planes, trains and journeys often show up around life changes. Missing one can mirror hesitation about moving on.
Perfectionism
If you are usually punctual and organised, the dream may play out the very thing you work hardest to avoid.
questions: Where were you trying to go, and does it remind you of anything?
Do you feel behind in some part of life right now?
What kept getting in the way?

name: An exam or test
title: Dreaming of an exam or test
description: Why people dream about exams they haven't studied for, years after leaving school, and what these dreams can reflect.
intro: Many adults still dream of sitting an exam they forgot to study for, finding the wrong paper, or being unable to find the room. These dreams can return decades after school ends.
themes: Being evaluated
Exams stand for being judged. The dream may surface before a review, an interview or any moment you feel tested.
Unpreparedness
Not knowing the answers can mirror feeling out of your depth in a new role or responsibility.
High standards
People who push themselves hard often report these dreams, even when they are well prepared in waking life.
Old patterns
Returning to school in a dream can point to an old pressure or belief that still shapes you.
questions: Is there a test, review or big moment coming up?
What subject or room was it, and does it bring anything to mind?
Did you actually fail, or wake before finding out?

name: Death or dying
title: Dreaming of death or dying
description: What dreams about your own death or someone else's death can mean. Usually these dreams are about change, not literal death.
intro: Dreaming about death, your own or someone else's, can be shocking. It helps to know that people across many traditions read death in dreams as an image of endings and change, not a prediction.
themes: An ending
A chapter closing, such as a job, a relationship, a home or a version of yourself, can show up as death.
Transformation
Death in dreams is often followed by something new. Notice what came after, if anything.
Worry about someone
Dreaming that a loved one dies can reflect care or concern for them, or fear of losing closeness.
Processing grief
If you have lost someone, death dreams can be part of how the mind works through it.
questions: What in your life is ending or changing right now?
Who died in the dream, and how do you feel about them lately?
Was the dream sad, peaceful or frightening?

name: An ex
title: Dreaming about your ex
description: Why you might dream about an ex-partner, even years later or when you are happy, and what these dreams can reflect.
intro: Dreaming about an ex is very common, including for people who are happy in a new relationship and have no wish to go back. The dream is often less about the person than about what they stood for.
themes: Unfinished feelings
Things left unsaid, or a breakup that never quite made sense, can resurface in dreams.
A pattern repeating
An ex can appear when a current situation echoes an old dynamic, in love, friendship or work.
A past version of you
The dream may be about who you were in that time of life, more than the other person.
Comparison
New relationships can stir memories of old ones. That is normal and does not mean something is wrong.
questions: What was happening in the dream between you?
Does anything in your life right now feel like that relationship did?
What do you miss, or not miss, about who you were then?

name: Being pregnant
title: Dreaming of being pregnant
description: What pregnancy dreams can mean for anyone, whether or not you are expecting, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: Pregnancy dreams happen to people of every age and gender, and to those who are not expecting or planning a baby at all. They often feel significant on waking.
themes: Something growing
A project, idea, business or relationship that is still developing can appear as a pregnancy.
Anticipation
Waiting for something big to arrive, with excitement or nerves, can take this shape.
Responsibility
Pregnancy can mirror a new duty or role you are preparing to take on.
Real life
If you are pregnant or hoping to be, these dreams are a very normal way the mind processes it.
questions: What in your life is growing or in the works?
Did the pregnancy feel joyful, surprising or worrying?
Is a new responsibility on its way?

name: A house or hidden rooms
title: Dreaming of a house or discovering new rooms
description: What house dreams can mean, including finding secret rooms, a childhood home, or a house falling apart.
intro: Houses are some of the richest dream settings. Many people describe finding a door they never noticed, rooms that keep going, or returning to a childhood home that looks slightly wrong.
themes: The self
A long tradition in dream reading treats the house as an image of yourself, with different rooms as different parts of your life.
Hidden rooms
Discovering new space often feels exciting. It can mirror untapped potential, or something you are just beginning to notice.
Childhood home
Old houses can bring back old feelings, memories and family dynamics.
Damage or decay
Leaks, cracks or crumbling walls can echo stress or something in life that needs attention.
questions: Whose house was it, and did you recognise it?
What did you find in the rooms?
How did being there feel?

name: A car out of control
title: Dreaming of a car out of control or brakes failing
description: What it can mean to dream your car's brakes fail, you can't steer, or someone else is driving.
intro: Brakes that don't work, a steering wheel that won't turn, or sitting in the back seat with nobody driving: car dreams often capture a very specific kind of panic.
themes: Control and direction
Cars carry us through life. A car out of control can mirror feeling that life's direction is not in your hands.
Who is driving
If someone else was at the wheel, consider whether another person has too much say in your choices.
Moving too fast
Failing brakes can echo a pace you cannot slow down, such as a busy schedule or a fast-moving situation.
Responsibility
Crashing or nearly crashing may reflect a fear of making a costly mistake.
questions: Who was driving the car?
Where were you heading, and did you get there?
Is there something in life moving faster than you would like?

name: Spiders
title: Dreaming of spiders
description: What spider dreams can mean, from fear and feeling trapped to patience and creativity, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: Spiders in dreams can appear alone or in swarms, on the wall or on your skin. For people who fear them, these dreams can be intense. For others, the spider is a quieter, stranger presence.
themes: Feeling trapped
Webs can mirror situations that feel sticky or hard to get out of.
Something creeping in
Small worries that multiply can show up as spiders appearing everywhere.
Patience and creation
Spiders build carefully. Some traditions link them to creativity and to weaving your own story.
Plain fear
If you dislike spiders when awake, the dream may simply be your mind's way of showing anxiety.
questions: Was there a web, and were you caught in it?
Is there a situation that feels hard to untangle?
Were you frightened, or simply watching?

name: Dogs
title: Dreaming of dogs
description: What dreams about dogs can mean, including friendly dogs, a dog attacking, or a lost pet.
intro: Dogs appear often in dreams, as beloved pets, strays, or occasionally as a threat. The meaning tends to depend on how the dog behaved and what dogs mean to you.
themes: Loyalty and friendship
A friendly dog can reflect trust, companionship, or someone who has your back.
Protection
A guard dog may point to boundaries, being protected, or wanting to protect someone.
Conflict
A dog that bites or attacks can mirror tension with someone close, or a betrayal you fear.
A pet you have lost
Dreaming of a pet who has died is a common and often comforting way of remembering them.
questions: Was the dog friendly, scared or aggressive?
Did you know the dog?
Who in your life feels loyal, or not, right now?

name: Cats
title: Dreaming of cats
description: What cat dreams can mean, from independence and intuition to mystery, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: Cats in dreams can feel affectionate, aloof or mysterious. Many people associate them with independence, intuition and a certain wildness.
themes: Independence
A cat can stand for doing things your own way, or a wish for more freedom.
Intuition
Cats are often linked to instinct and quiet awareness, a reminder to trust your gut.
Comfort
A cat curled up with you can mirror a need for rest, warmth or self-care.
Distrust
A hissing or scratching cat may reflect someone you are unsure about, or feeling unwelcome.
questions: How did the cat treat you?
Is your intuition telling you something you have been ignoring?
Do you need more independence or more comfort right now?

name: Fire
title: Dreaming of fire
description: What dreams about fire, a burning house, or flames can mean, from anger and passion to renewal.
intro: Fire in dreams can be destructive, like a burning house or a wildfire, or warm, like a fireplace or candle. Its meaning often depends on whether it was under control.
themes: Strong emotion
Fire can mirror anger, passion or frustration that feels hard to contain.
Destruction and renewal
Something burning down can feel like loss, but fire also clears the way for new growth.
Urgency
An emergency can reflect a problem you feel has to be dealt with now.
Warmth
A fire under control can stand for comfort, connection and energy.
questions: Was the fire under control or spreading?
What was burning?
Is there anger or passion you have been keeping in?

name: A tsunami or giant wave
title: Dreaming of a tsunami or giant wave
description: What tsunami dreams can mean, from feeling overwhelmed to big change on the horizon, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: A huge wave rising on the horizon, and the dread of knowing it is coming, is a memorable dream. Some people run, some watch, and some are swept up.
themes: Overwhelm
Like drowning dreams, a tsunami can mirror stress that feels like it will wash everything away.
Change you can see coming
A wave in the distance can stand for a change you know is on its way, such as a move, a birth or a deadline.
Emotional release
Big waves can reflect feelings that have built up for a long time.
Surviving it
Many people find the wave passes or they float. That can be reassuring to notice.
questions: Did you see the wave coming?
What big change is on your horizon?
Were you alone, or with other people?

name: Being lost
title: Dreaming of being lost
description: What dreams about being lost in a city, building or forest can mean, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: Wandering through streets you don't recognise, corridors that loop back, or a forest with no path: being lost is a common dream and often a frustrating one.
themes: Lack of direction
Being lost can mirror uncertainty about where life, work or a relationship is heading.
A big decision
When you are torn between options, the mind can turn it into a maze.
New territory
A new job, city or stage of life can feel like streets with no map.
Looking for something
Notice what or who you were searching for. It may be what you need.
questions: What were you trying to find?
Is there a decision you are stuck on?
Did you find your way in the end?

name: Not being able to run or scream
title: Dreaming you can't run, move or scream
description: Why you might dream you can't run, move, scream or call for help, and what these dreams can reflect.
intro: Legs that feel like lead, a scream that makes no sound, a phone you can't dial. These dreams of being unable to act are frustrating and very common.
themes: Feeling powerless
Many people link these dreams to a situation where they feel they can't change the outcome.
Not being heard
A silent scream can mirror feeling ignored or unable to speak up.
The sleeping body
During REM sleep the body is naturally paralysed so we don't act out dreams. The dream may weave this real sensation into the story.
Hesitation
Being stuck can echo holding back from a step you know you need to take.
questions: Where in life do you feel unable to act?
Who did you want to call or warn?
Have you been holding your voice back lately?

name: A partner cheating
title: Dreaming your partner is cheating
description: Why you might dream your partner cheats on you, and what these dreams usually reflect. They rarely mean it is happening.
intro: Waking up from a dream that your partner cheated can leave you upset with them, even though they did nothing. These dreams are common and, on their own, are not evidence of anything.
themes: Insecurity
The dream may reflect fear of losing someone, or feeling less important to them.
Feeling left out
If your partner has been busy or distant, the dream may express feeling sidelined, by work, family or a hobby.
Past hurt
Old betrayals, yours or someone else's, can surface in a new relationship.
Your own wishes
Sometimes it is less about the partner and more about a part of life you want more of.
questions: Have you felt distant from your partner lately?
Who was the other person, and what do they represent to you?
Is an old hurt resurfacing?

name: A baby
title: Dreaming of a baby
description: What baby dreams can mean, including finding, holding or forgetting a baby, plus questions to reflect on.
intro: Babies show up in dreams in many forms: holding a newborn, finding a baby somewhere unexpected, or the anxious dream of forgetting one.
themes: A new beginning
A baby can stand for a fresh start, a new project, or a new side of yourself.
Vulnerability
Babies need care. The dream may reflect something in your life that feels fragile.
Responsibility
Forgetting or losing a baby is a common stress dream when there is a lot to keep track of.
Nurturing
Caring for a baby can mirror a wish to look after others, or to be looked after.
questions: Whose baby was it?
What new thing in your life needs care right now?
Did you feel calm, joyful or anxious?

name: A wedding
title: Dreaming of a wedding
description: What wedding dreams can mean, including your own wedding, marrying a stranger, or a wedding going wrong.
intro: Wedding dreams can be joyful, chaotic or surreal: marrying a stranger, forgetting the dress, or arriving at the wrong ceremony. They often appear around commitments of any kind.
themes: Commitment
A wedding can mirror a promise you are making, to a person, a job or a plan.
Union
Bringing two things together, such as two parts of your life or two ideas, can show up as a marriage.
Pressure and expectations
A wedding going wrong can echo worry about meeting other people's expectations.
Real plans
If a wedding is coming up, these dreams are a normal way of processing the excitement and stress.
questions: Who were you marrying, if anyone?
What commitment is on your mind?
Did the day go to plan?

name: A loved one who has died
title: Dreaming of a loved one who has died
description: What it can mean to dream of a parent, grandparent, friend or pet who has passed away, and how these dreams can help with grief.
intro: Dreams of someone who has died are among the most meaningful dreams people describe. They can feel comforting, sad, ordinary, or startlingly real.
themes: Grief
Dreams are one of the ways the mind processes loss, sometimes for years afterwards.
Comfort and connection
Many people wake feeling they had a visit, a chance to see someone again or say something left unsaid.
Guidance
The person may appear when you face a choice they would have had an opinion on.
Anniversaries
These dreams often cluster around birthdays, holidays and the date of the loss.
questions: What did they say or do in the dream?
How did you feel when you woke up?
Is there something you would like to tell them?
